newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-PENULTIMATE JUMP GIVES KASPARKOVA GOLD.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-PENULTIMATE JUMP GIVES KASPARKOVA GOLD.

text.p: Czech Sarka Kasparkova recorded the third longest triple jump in the fledgling history of the women's sport to win gold at the world championships on Monday.
Kasparkova, who took bronze last year in Atlanta, where women's triple jump was first introduced in Olympics, jumped 15.20 metres with her penultimate attempt.
Only Ukraine's Inessa Kravets, who holds the world's two best marks of 15.50 and 15.33, has jumped further.
Kravets, the Olympic and world champion, was absent for Saturday's qualifying round.
Romania's Rodica Mateescu, who led the event until Kasparkova's winning leap of 15.16 metres set at her first attempt, had to settle for silver. Ukrainian Yelena Govorova took bronze with 14.67.
"After Rodica's first try over 15 metres, I didn't panic," said the 26-year-old Kasparkova, who had a previous best of 14.98 metres. "I knew I had five more jumps left.
"Coming third in Atlanta boosted my confidence and I knew I could make a medal. "I didn't know exactly how far I could jump but I had to go very far to win so I just tried my best."
Mateescu, who had victory in sight when Kasparkova produced her winning jump, said she had mixed feelings about her silver medal.
"I'm disappointed to have missed the gold and at the same time, I'm satisfied with my performance," said Mateescu, who set a national record.
Govorova's third place was met by boos from a partisan crowd, upset to see local hope Olga Vasdeki, who came fourth with 14.62 metres, lose a medal by five centimetres.
"The reaction of the crowd came as a surprise and made me a little bit angry," she said. "Apart from that, I'm ever so happy."
